chunks: Saad narrated from al-Husayn ibn Ali, from Ahmad ibn Hilal, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him: A handkerchief used for wiping (with it), is it permissible for a man to place it on his shoulder or wrap it as a lower garment and pray? He said: 'There is no harm.'

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no harm / It is permissible
key_terms.مِنْدِيلٌ: A handkerchief or cloth used for wiping
key_terms.يَتَّزِرَ بِهِ: To wrap it as a lower garment (izar)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to wear a used cleaning cloth as clothing during prayer?
ai.summary: In this narration from Sahih al-Tusi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the ritual purity and validity of using a 'mandil'—a cloth typically used for personal hygiene or wiping—as valid prayer attire. The Imam’s affirmative response ('la ba'sa') indicates that as long as the cloth adequately covers the awrah, its prior use for istinja or general cleaning does not invalidate the prayer, reflecting the Shia juristic principle that minor impurities or prior utility do not preclude a garment from being worn in salat.
